newsitem.title: CHINA: Trial of China dissident Wang to start Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Trial of China dissident Wang to start Wednesday.

text.p: Prominent Chinese dissident Wang Dan will go on trial on Wednesday on the capital charge of plotting to overthrow the government, a family member said on Friday.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court informed Wang's family that his trial would start on Wednesday, the relative said by telephone.
Court officials could not be reached for comment.
"As for family members, only Wang Dan's father and his sister will be able to attend," she said.

Court officials have confirmed that former student leader Wang, detained since May 1995, has been charged with plotting to overthrow the government -- a crime that carries a maximum penalty of death and a minimum of 10 years in prison.
They have not given further details of the trial, though one official said Wang could appeal to the Higher People's Court if convicted.
The court was widely expected to fill the limited number of courtroom seats with carefully selected people to keep away foreign reporters and fellow dissidents.

If last year's trial of Wei Jingsheng, father of China's democracy movement, was an indication, Wang's court appearance would be kept from public view, a political activist said. Dissidents and foreign reporters were barred from Wei's trial.
Wei, a nominee for this year's Nobel Peace Prize, was jailed for 15 years in 1979 and had been parolled for less than a year before being detained again in April 1994.
Last December he was sentenced to a further 14 years in prison for subversion and for funding democracy activists.

Wang, 26, has already served four years in prison for counter-revolutionary crimes, or subversion, for his role in pro-democracy demonstrations which were crushed by the army in June 1989 with heavy loss of life.
Relatives said they had found a lawyer willing to defend Wang after being given one day to do so.
Wang's mother, Wang Lingyun, a 61-year-old museum researcher who has no background in law, has said she would defend her son in court. Chinese law allows an accused to be defended by a family member.
The dissident was very calm and mentally prepared for a harsh sentence, Wang's mother has said.

Wang Dan had been active after being released on parole in 1993, defying persistent police surveillance to join in a daring appeal to communist leaders for the release of all those still in prison for their part in the 1989 protests.
